Phones open a web page, no install. Our Bun relay links them to the TV and voices every creature with Kokoro, on a Mac at home.
Our open-source library, doodle-cutout, turns a phone photo into a clean sticker, right in the phone's browser.
Claude reads the drawing and decides how it plays. Its prompt asks for five-year-old-safe answers, and every field is checked before the TV sees it.
Engineering observations on the virtual device, not Fire TV hardware: first frame in two thirds of a second, memory well under the limit.
Races sometimes froze at the start; the crash dump showed a watchdog deadlock. After the fix, a hundred and five starts on the virtual device, zero freezes.
It's for families with kids four to ten. Little ones race with a visible speed boost. Under two cents a creature, first names only, no accounts.
